doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

chapter: Youth, war and the Armstrong club
title: Jacobs's girlfriends and teenage music tastes
summary: Her friends thought her jazz interest wacky; popular acts were Bing Crosby, the Boswell Sisters and Arthur Godfrey-style singers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I couldn’t agree more. It really has so much cultural legacy and it makes absolute sense that you learn it through the music and blues also.
Phoebe, I’m curious when you were oh let’s say 18 or 19, did your girlfriends think that your interest in jazz music was a little out of the ordinary?
Of course. They all thought I was wacky. They couldn’t believe it.
At that time what was the normal teenager into music-wise?

Well you know you’re going back a long time, you know, but I’m no baby. Like who was big in those days, Bing Crosby, who was the guy that did — oh a lot of romantic singers or people that you might get on Arthur Godfrey’s show or something like that. Of course the one outstanding one is Bing Crosby as far as I was concerned. The Boswell Sisters were coming up, groups of that type.
